summary: Iteration 76 — verified the massive Dev OS simplification: (a) single @devmanager agent consolidation across backend + frontend, (b) 5-tab Build Room with quick actions + Builders. Backend 9/9 pytest passing on /app/backend/tests/test_iteration76_devmgr_consolidation.py (roles endpoint returns exactly 1 devmgr entry, @devmanager mention triggers a single devmgr reply, legacy tokens @architect/@qa route ONLY to devmgr, @devmanager 'build me a habit tracker' auto-created dev_project + preview HTML served, POST /code-review posts an '@devmanager' trigger + queues devmgr reply, POST /talk works without role_key, dev-tasks CRUD lifecycle green, publish + public /api/p/{slug}/index.html serve). Frontend (Playwright on real preview URL): DevStudio at /dev-os/projects/77511f35.../studio renders with exactly the 4 desktop tabs (Preview/Tasks/Files/Release) — Chat tab is present in DOM but has md:hidden so it's not visible on desktop. Chat is the left pane. All 5 quick-action chips render; 🐛 Fix Bug prefills ds-input with 'Fix this bug: ' (does NOT auto-send). Builders menu opens and shows all 7 builder options (logic/roles/data/workflow/form/report/integration). Data Model builder dialog opens with builder-field-thing/-fields/-rel; ds-submit disabled until required (thing+fields) filled; submit fires the composed instruction 'Add a new data model "Customers" with fields: name, email, phone, status. Build the list view, add/edit forms and a detail view for it, wired into the navigation.' into ds-chat-log. Tasks tab adds a task (ds-task-input + ds-task-add) → ds-task-row appears → ds-task-advance moves status to 'In progress'. Files tab shows generated project files (frontend/index.html etc). Release tab shows ds-release-panel with ds-release-publish, ds-release-vercel, ds-env-add, ds-env-save. Route /dev-os/projects/{id} (no /studio) redirects to /studio. /dev-os/agents route removed (redirects to /). /dev-os hub does NOT show 'AI Engineering Team' card. Chat @mention popover in dev chat d553cda0 with 'typing @dev' shows ONLY mention-option-devmgr (Dev Manager · @devmanager) — no architect/qa/frontend specialist entries. Latest AI replies to code-review are ALL sender ai-agent-devmgr, confirming no specialist cascade. ONE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUE (not a code bug): EMERGENT_LLM_KEY has hit the $20 budget cap during this session ('litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 20.02, Max budget: 20.001'), so a follow-up plain-actionable-comment regression test ('please change the footer background to a soft pastel blue' in the dev chat) did not produce a Dev Manager reply within 150s — the code path is verified correct (_should_implicit_devmgr → _looks_actionable('please change …') → True via lead-in strip + edit verb 'change '), and the talk_to_build call was invoked (visible in backend logs) but failed on the LLM budget cap. All earlier tests in this iteration already exercised the same auto-devmgr LLM path successfully before the budget hit.
action_items: ENVIRONMENTAL (not a code fix): EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget cap ($20.001) has been reached — future @devmanager / talk_to_build calls will fail with 'Budget has been exceeded' until the key is topped up or rotated. Main agent should verify this is expected in the dev preview environment; production keys should have higher caps. All Dev-Manager code paths are wired correctly; only the LLM call itself fails.

LOW: Historical messages in chat d553cda0 from the pre-consolidation era still contain replies from ai-agent-frontend / ai-agent-designer / ai-agent-qa etc. These are correct history and NOT a regression — MessageBubble renders them fine — but if the product wants a clean 'single-@devmanager brand' timeline, consider a one-off migration that rewrites those old sender_ids to ai-agent-devmgr (metadata.role_original = frontend etc.). Purely cosmetic.
critical_code_review_comments: services/dev_chat_agents.py at 987 lines is over the 700-line soft cap. It now cleanly owns the single-agent domain — consider splitting the LLM-idea-generation helpers (_llm_build_ideas + _FALLBACK_IDEAS + _tokens/_is_continuation heuristics) into a sibling module dev_chat_ideas.py so the core dispatcher (parse_role_mentions, dispatch_role_replies, _should_implicit_devmgr) stays under 500 lines.

routes/dev_os.py at 2074 lines is far over the 700-line soft cap and mixes projects, tasks, proposals, files, snapshots, presence, preview, publish, code-review and talk-to-build. Consider splitting per-domain: dev_projects.py, dev_tasks.py, dev_files.py, dev_presence.py, dev_talk.py — each becomes a focused router.

MentionPopover.jsx dev-chat popover already correctly shows exactly one entry post-consolidation, but the roster-trigger branch also drops the 'dev' key row (r.key !== 'dev'). Since ROLES no longer contains a 'dev' key at all, this filter is dead code — remove for clarity.

DevStudio.jsx has Chat tab in TABS array with mobileOnly:true and CSS md:hidden, but data-testid=ds-tab-chat is still emitted on the desktop DOM (just hidden by CSS). This is arguably correct because it's the same button; tests that check 'tab present on mobile' will find it via testid. Consider a comment above TABS documenting the mobileOnly semantic so future refactors don't accidentally remove the testid.

DevStudio.jsx line 108 submit() posts to /dev-projects/{id}/talk without any role_key, matching the new server contract. Nice cleanup — the TalkToBuildRequest schema on the server can drop role_key from Optional entirely (it's now unused code).

TasksPanel.jsx loading state renders 'Loading tasks…' WITHOUT the ds-tasks-panel testid — testing agents (including me) hit a race where the tab click lands before the fetch resolves. Consider adding data-testid='ds-tasks-panel' to BOTH the loading placeholder AND the loaded panel so waits are deterministic.

BuildersMenu.jsx dispatches builder.compose(clean) values through a chain of user-input strings; no escaping — a user could paste text containing '```' or '{' that breaks the LLM prompt. Consider clipping each field to ~200 chars and stripping newlines before compose.

PROTECTED_VARIABLES: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget of $20 max is very low for a QA/prod workspace — a single build_project + a few /talk calls can burn through it in one session. Consider bumping the cap and/or exposing a soft-warning banner when balance falls below $2.
